subject: Quantize + prefetch: billing flooring and token-accounting implications
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@finwave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on quantization / prefetch impact to monthly minimums

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked promising. Procurement is working through the SOW and we hit a couple of billing questions that finance needs cleared before we can sign:

1) If we move to a quantized model (int8/int4) provided by Redwood, how does that affect token-based billing and the application of minimums? Specifically: do quantized variants get billed at the same token rates, and are there any "quantize discounts" that change the minimum-floor math?

2) We use aggressive KV prefetching on our side (warm prefixes) to reduce latency. Would those prefetched tokens be treated like regular tokens for context-length aggregation, or is there a different amortization / crediting treatment for cached prefixes?

3) Rounding: our accounting wants a short explainer and examples showing how the monthly floor would be applied across many short bursts (microbursts), and whether per-call rounding could cause invoices to materially exceed actual token usage.

Can you send a short write-up and any sample invoice scenarios? Procurement would like to run this by finance by EOD next Thursday.

Appreciate it,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Procurement, FinWave
samira@finwave.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finwave.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on quantization / prefetch impact to monthly minimums

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise explainer and attached a spreadsheet with three sample invoice scenarios (short-burst-heavy, steady-streaming, and amortized-prefix case). Short answers up front, details below:

- Quantization: model quantization (int8/int4) changes compute cost on our side but does NOT change the token metering unit. Tokens are still the metering primitive. We do provide recommended pricing adjustments for dedicated/commit customers where we can guarantee certain throughput/latency; any explicit per-token discount for a quantized model must be negotiated and appears as a line-item (not an automatic rate change).

- Prefetch / KV-warm prefixes: Prefetched tokens are treated as part of the active conversation context when they are material to a request (i.e., they occupy context slots). We do have a prefix-credit program for long-lived shared prefixes that can be negotiated (amortized prefix credits) — that reduces billable token count in the invoice allocation step, but it’s a contract-level concession rather than automatic free tokens.

- Rounding and minimums: We apply a monthly-floor at the invoice level. Internal per-request rounding happens to the nearest token quantum for metering, then we aggregate across the billing window and apply minima. The important effect: many sub-token or sub-quantum microbursts get aggregated and compared against the monthly floor; however, per-call rounding can cause small drift. The attached sheet shows math for: (A) pure per-call rounding without aggregation, (B) aggregating then applying floor, and (C) a smoothing concession for pilot customers.

What I attached:
- FinWave_pricing_scenarios_v3.xlsx (scenarios + math)
- prefetch-kv-examples.csv (sample request logs showing prefix reuse)

Next steps: Vanessa (cc’d) runs the concessions/commit math and Karthik will propose language we can put in the SOW about amortized prefix credits and a quantization discount clause. We can also produce a sample invoice for the exact FinWave 30-day trace you shared during the pilot if that helps.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if that speeds review.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finwave.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on quantization / prefetch impact to monthly minimums

Hi Samira — looping in the concessions and pricing team notes. A few concrete items and a worked example below.

Summary answers:
- Quantize discount: we can offer a 12-month commit discount (example below) that effectively reduces the per-token invoice rate for quantized variants by a negotiated percent; this is represented as a credit line on the invoice (so it doesn't change the metering semantics).
- Prefix amortization: we can provide a negotiated amortized-prefix credit for prefixes that are deterministically reused (e.g., a shared knowledge base prompt). The credit is computed as: expected prefix reuses per month * prefix token length * discount factor. Credits are applied during invoice post-processing.
- Rounding smoothing: for pilots and early-stage customers we can apply a rounding-smoothing concession that caps per-invoice rounding drift to N% of total usage for the billing month.

Worked example (excerpt from spreadsheet):
- FinWave baseline trace: 1,200,000 billable tokens (raw metering after per-call quantization rounding).
- Monthly floor (contract): 1,000,000 tokens.
- If per-call rounding pushes aggregate to 1,015,400 tokens, you would be billed for 1,015,400 unless a smoothing concession applies.
- With a negotiated 8% quantize discount on per-token charge and a prefix-credit of 12k tokens/month, net charge looks like: billed_tokens = 1,015,400 - 12,000 (prefix) = 1,003,400; net_rate = base_rate * 0.92; invoiced_amount = billed_tokens * net_rate.

Vanessa’s ask: if FinWave is willing to commit to a 12-month minimum (3.5M tokens / quarter), we can build in:
- 8% quantize discount on the per-token unit for the agreed models;
- 12k/mo amortized prefix credit for known warm prefixes;
- a 1.5% rounding-smoothing cap for the first 3 invoices after go-live.

I attached a version of the proposal in the spreadsheet. If that sounds reasonable, Karthik can translate into SOW language and pricing table.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@finwave.com>

Subject: Re: Question on quantization / prefetch impact to monthly minimums

Vanessa / Marcus — thanks for the clear write-up and examples. A few follow-ups from finance/procurement:

- The amortized prefix credit sounds useful. Can you confirm how prefixes are declared / validated? We need an auditable mapping (prefix id, token length, owner) that our auditors can reconcile to usage logs.

- For the quantize discount: your example looks reasonable. Procurement would prefer the discount to be a rate-tier (applied only to tokens attributed to quantized model calls) rather than a flat invoice credit. Can you confirm whether you can show token-level line-items on the invoice (e.g., "quantized-model X usage: 320k tokens @ $Y/token")?

- On the commit: FinWave would be open to a 12-month commit with a clause that allows a one-time renegotiation at the 6 month mark if observed usage patterns deviate by >20%.

If you can confirm the prefix validation process and provide a draft SOW clause for the quantize-discount and renegotiation trigger, we can route to legal. Can Karthik own the SOW draft?

Best,
Samira

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finwave.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 16:58:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on quantization / prefetch impact to monthly minimums

Hi Samira — thanks, looping in legal PR for final SOW formatting. Quick answers and next steps below; I attached a draft SOW clause and a DocuSign-ready pricing appendix.

1) Prefix validation: process we propose — FinWave submits a CSV of declared prefixes (prefix_id, canonical_text, expected_token_length, claim_owner). Redwood runs a 30-day verification against production request logs to validate reuse frequency. If prefix reuse >= threshold (we typically use >= 5 reuses/day average) we mark prefix eligible for amortized credit. Both parties retain verification logs for audit. We'll include the exact audit log fields in the SOW.

2) Invoice line-items: yes — we can show per-model line items including a separate line for quantized-model usage. The discount can be defined as a per-model rate tier in the pricing appendix (so it appears in the invoice calculation rather than an opaque credit).

3) Commit renegotiation clause: included in the attached draft SOW — a single mutual-review window at month-6 if observed billed tokens deviate by >20% from projected usage; outcome: either (a) adjust rate/credits for remainder term, or (b) revert to month-to-month with a 30-day notice.

Attached: FW-Docusign-proposal.pdf (pricing appendix, SOW snippet), FinWave_pricing_scenarios_v3.xlsx (updated with exact numbers for the SOW), DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/prepare/fw-proposal-2026

If this matches what you need, I can get Legal to finalize and push to DocuSign by EOD Monday.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
snippet: Quantization doesn't change token metering; prefix credits and invoice line-items can be negotiated. See attached scenarios and draft SOW.
